headline: Aerobic efficiency gain is now confirmed by HR data — easy-run HR has dropped meaningfully on comparable efforts.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The HR trend flagged last time has resolved clearly in your favour. Easy-run HR on comparable efforts has dropped substantially over the recent block, which is a concrete signal that aerobic adaptation is tracking the volume increase rather than just absorbing it. That's the most meaningful single datapoint right now.

Volume continues to build at a controlled rate, and the 20-week running streak — now matching your personal best — reflects the consistency that underpins both of those. The streak itself isn't the goal, but unbroken structural habit at this volume is exactly the kind of base that compounds into ultra durability.

The one thing worth holding in view: strength session frequency has nudged slightly lower in the recent block. A small dip during a volume-building phase is unremarkable, but it's worth keeping an eye on whether that pattern continues as running load holds elevated.
watch_items: Watch whether the easy-run HR improvement continues to hold as weekly volume stays elevated — a plateau here would be informative.
Monitor strength session frequency over the coming weeks to catch any further drift while running load is high.
Zone 2 volume is sitting well below the target range — worth noticing whether this is a structural gap or a consequence of how sessions are being distributed.
Sleep data is too sparse to draw conclusions yet, but as tracking accumulates, watch for any pattern between low-score nights and next-day aerobic HR.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 145 km vs 125 km prior block (+16%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 146 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 7 vs 6 runs)
